_doc: Optional `tend_lines` (FOLK-043, 1-3 strings <= 140 chars, {player}/{name}): what a Sworn friend says when they tend your injuries (family.json folk_visits.tend). Optional `drop_by_lines` (FOLK-041, 1-3 strings <= 140 chars, {player}/{name}): what a Close friend says when they leave you a gift (family.json folk_visits.drop_by). Named NPCs. Optional `lend_lines` (C-404, 1-3 strings <= 140 chars, {player}) are what they say, one picked at random, right after the lend-a-hand message. Optional `activity` (GFX-219, one of sweep/hoe/fish/read/hawk/chop/sit) is the two-frame prop they work with while idle; a working NPC stays at home (see WorkProps). Optional `birthday` {month 1..12, day 1..30} gives a named NPC a yearly birthday (FOLK-022; without it a named NPC has none, generated villagers get a hashed one) optional `player_birthday_line` (FOLK-029, <=160 chars, {player}) is what they say on the PLAYER's birthday instead of the shared folk_greetings.player_birthday pick, and optional `birthday_line` (<=160 chars, {player}) is what they say that day instead of the shared folk_greetings.birthday pool. Optional `festival_lines` (FOLK-025) {festival world-event id (festival: true in world_events.json): line (<=160 chars, {player})} is what they say when you chat during that festival in their region, once per festival per year (birthdays win), instead of the shared family.json folk_greetings.festival pool. Optional `taught_dish_line` (COOK-003, <= 160 chars, must contain {dish}) is what a friend who taught you a dish (a `learn_dish` lesson) says in their next chat within 14 days of the first time you cook it, once per dish, +3 favor. Optional `player_birthday_gift` (FOLK-030) {item (items.json id), count 1..3} is handed over with their own player_birthday_line (same once-a-year flag). Optional `graduation_line` (SPAR-002, string <= 160 chars) is the line a teacher says when a bout masters the style they taught you (generic line when absent). Optional `lessons` [{tier (index into family.json folk_tiers, >= 1, strictly rising, max 3), text (<=220 chars, {name}/{player}), effects (only learn_recipe, learn_dish (COOK-001, a taught home meal), learn_technique, profession_xp, attributes 1..2, dao_insight, practice_days 1..10, items)}] are taught once, one a day per NPC, when you talk at that tier (FOLK-020). Each becomes a CharacterData at session start and lives on: it ages, cultivates off-screen (if 'cultivates') at its region's qi density times 'diligence' (fraction of days spent cultivating, default 0.3), attempts breakthroughs and can die of old age. realm is a realm id; roots map element ids to purity (omit to roll randomly); attributes default to 10. region/pos/size/color place the NPC in the world. gender (optional) is a data/names.json gender; surname/given_name are optional (name stays the display name). NPCs generated at runtime (Npcs.spawn) have no entry here. dialogue is a file id in data/dialogue/. likes/dislikes (GIFT-001, optional): lists of item ids or item tags; a gift matching a like is worth family.json acquaintance.gift_like_mult times as much, a dislike costs gift_dislike_favor (a dislike wins when both match). Validated against items.json ids and tags. deed_context (optional) also offers deeds from data/deeds.json. bloodline (optional) is a data/bloodlines.json id the NPC carries (and may pass to children). hunter (WILD-017, optional bool): the NPC leads their region's village hunt (VillageHunt.hunter_of): named in the notice, +2 more favor on a win. Optional `spots` (FOLK-017, named NPCs with a region): {work, market, rain, festival: [x, y] inside the region map; rest_weekday: a weekday name}. Folk.spot_for picks where the NPC stands today: a running festival (the festival spot, else near the region festival_square) > rain or storm (rain) > rest_weekday (stays at pos) > a market day of the region (market) > work > pos; a missing spot falls through. Optional top-level "scenes" (FOLK-013): [{id (unique), npc (a named npc id or "any_villager"), min_favor (a family.json folk_tiers min), text (1-3 sentences, {name} = the villager), gift (optional items.json id), weather (optional non-empty list of Weather kinds: clear, cloudy, rain, snow, fog, storm; the scene plays only on such a day in the region you stand in, FOLK-021)}]; shown once, at most one a day, when you talk to the villager. Optional top-level "errands" (GUIDE-003) feed the journal: {npc: named npc id, asked_flag, done_flag, text}; listed while the asked flag is set and the done flag is not.

sect_join: The {sect}, is it? Walls and rules, {player}. I left them, but they teach well. Keep the road under your feet.
Sixty years ago I wore a sect's colours too. Whatever the {sect} is, {player}, do not let it name you.
promotion: {rank} now. An old man's tea tastes sweeter for it, {player}. Mind the pride that rides with the title.

tend_lines: Mo lays a warm palm over the hurt and counts your breath until it evens out. 'Slow, {player}. The body mends at the pace it chooses.'
Mo grinds a pinch of old mugwort into a paste and binds it on with a strip of scroll-cloth. 'Paper heals what pride breaks, {player}.'
drop_by_lines: Mo left a withered mugwort bundle on your step: 'Old paper and old herbs keep each other company, {player}.'
Something was left at your door by Mo, wrapped in scrap paper: 'Too much for one old man, {player}. Take it.'
lend_lines: Mo squints over a scroll. "You sort better than my old disciples did, {player}. They only ever sorted themselves."
"Dust is only slow time, {player}," Mo says. "You have cleared a good deal of it today."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, another year on your road. Sit a while; an old man is allowed to say he is glad you were born.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {player}, the drums fade and the lanterns burn down, but a walk beside you is what I will keep from {festival}. Old men hoard such things.

festival_lines.lantern_festival: {player}, on lantern night we set old grudges on the water. Mine sank long ago; light one with me and watch it go.
festival_lines.dragon_boat_festival: {player}, sixty festivals and I still cannot paddle in time. Come, beat the drum with me.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}, another year on these old bones, and the tea is still hot. Sit with me.

lessons.text: {name} sits you down in the lee of the shrine wall and teaches you to count your breath until the counting stops. "Slow is not weak, child."
{name} says nothing for a long while, then lets you hear what the breath sounds like when it is truly even. "There. Keep that."

npcs.name: Elder Mo
npcs.title: Retired Cultivator

sect_join: {player}! The {sect}! Grandmother says I shout too loud, but you joined the {sect}! Will you still visit?
You joined the {sect}?! Is it grand? Do they feed you? Grandmother is already packing food for you.
promotion: {rank}! {player}, you are a {rank}! I told everyone at the well. Now do not forget to come home for the lantern game.

tend_lines: Ling dabs a honeyed salve on the wound, scolding the whole time. 'You never rest, {player}! Sit. Grandmother says so, and so do I.'
Ling wraps the hurt in clean linen, tongue between her teeth. 'There. Don't tell Grandmother how I fussed, {player}.'
drop_by_lines: Ling left a little parcel on your sill: 'Grandmother says I made too many, {player}. Eat before they go stale!'
Ling slipped something by your door with a note: 'I was passing, {player}, and it made me think of you.'
lend_lines: Ling grins and wipes her hands on her apron. "With you it goes twice as fast, {player}. Grandmother will be amazed."
"Same time next week?" Ling asks. "I will save the dull jobs for you, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, it is your birthday! Grandmother says I may not bake, so I made you a riddle instead. Many happy returns!
npcs.taught_dish_line: You made {dish}, the way I showed you? Did the steam come out slow? Grandmother says that is the only secret. Was it good? Tell me it was good!

festival_lines.lantern_festival: {player}! I wrote a riddle for the lantern game and nobody has solved it. You try! No, wait, don't tell Grandmother the answer.
festival_lines.dragon_boat_festival: {player}! Did you try the rice dumplings? I wrapped the sweet ones myself, so don't scowl.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}! Do you know what day it is? Grandmother made too much, so you are staying to eat.

lessons.text: {name} shows you how she steams eggs and well water slow and low until the custard shivers like a pond, then sends you home with a bowl of broth.
{name} lifts a hot lid and shows you Grandmother's honey egg cake, every fold of it. "Don't tell anyone how little honey. Now it's yours too."

npcs.name: Xiao Ling
npcs.title: Childhood Friend

sect_join: Hm. The {sect}. Heard of them. Watch whoever walks behind you, {player}. Sects bite quiet.
Hm. So you joined the {sect}. Sound enough, or not, I'll judge by what you do. Keep your back to a wall.
promotion: Hm. {rank}. They saw what I saw, then. Good. Don't let it make you slow, {player}.

tend_lines: Ma binds the wound the way he binds his own, tight with a strip of hide. 'A hunter walks home on it, {player}. So will you.'
Ma packs the cut with moss and pine resin without a word, then grunts. 'Next time watch your footing, {player}.'
drop_by_lines: Ma left a bundle by your door: 'Took more than I can carry home, {player}. Do not argue.'
Ma's heavy hand left something at your threshold: 'Good game, good friend. Share it, {player}.'
lend_lines: Ma sets down the axe and nods once. "Good swing, {player}. Wood warms you twice, once chopping and once burning."
"Stack it dry side up," Ma grunts. "You learn quick, {player}. Come back before the first frost."
npcs.graduation_line: Hunter Ma lowers his fists. "Nothing left I can show you with those hands."
npcs.player_birthday_line: Hm. {player}. Birthday, I hear. Another year and you are still standing. Good. Keep at it.
npcs.taught_dish_line: Hm. Word is you cooked {dish}. Did you let it rest before you cut it? ...Good. A hunter who wastes no meat will never go hungry. Keep at it.

festival_lines.dragon_boat_festival: Hm. Loud, this boat business. But the river hasn't run so bright in years.
festival_lines.lantern_festival: Hm. Paper lights on the river. The deer would not understand it. I do. Stand by me a while, {player}.

npcs.birthday_line: Hm. {player}. The years pass like deer, quiet and gone. Stay for the fire tonight.

lessons.text: {name} crouches by the trail and shows you how to read a track and place your feet so the leaves stay silent, then roasts the boar you both carried home and shows you how to crackle the skin.
{name} walks you along the ridge at dusk, correcting your stance twice a step, until you move through the brush like a drifting shadow.

npcs.name: Hunter Ma
npcs.title: Village Hunter

tend_lines: Lan presses a poultice of bruised leaves to the wound. 'Hold still, {player}. The forest grows a cure beside every sting.'
Lan crushes two roots between her fingers and smooths the juice over the hurt. 'It will itch. That means it is working, {player}.'
drop_by_lines: Lan left a small bundle at your door: 'Picked at dawn, {player}. It was happier in your hands than in my basket.'
Lan tucked something by your door with a note: 'The forest gave twice today, {player}. Fair is fair.'
lend_lines: Lan smiles at the tidy shelves. "You handle the drying racks gently, {player}. Herbs remember that."
"A day with plants goes quiet and kind," Lan says. "Thank you for the company, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a birthday? Then take the first dew-grass of the morning. It is the freshest thing I own, and you earned it.
npcs.taught_dish_line: The forest told me you made {dish}. Of course it did. I hope you drank it warm, with no hurry; a cup left to cool teaches nothing.
npcs.birthday_line: Oh, {player}, you remembered? The forest gave me a good year. Have some tea, it is only leaf and kindness.

lessons.text: {name} copies out the way she mends torn channels with a simple pill, brushing the lines dry with her sleeve.
{name} presses a frostbell blossom into your palm. "Two of these, steeped slow, and no summer fever lasts. Nobody sells this; I kept it for a friend."

npcs.name: Herbalist Lan
npcs.title: Herb Gatherer

tend_lines: Qian sighs, produces a clean cloth from a sleeve and binds you up. 'This one is free, {player}. Do not make it a habit.'
Qian dresses the wound with brisk hands. 'Dead customers owe nothing, {player}. Stay alive; I have plans for you.'

lessons.text: {name} lets you hold the brass scales and teaches you to hear a false weight in the chain's chime. "Trust the ear, then the eye."
{name} unrolls a ledger and shows you how a debt is written so that it cannot be forgotten. He presses blank paper into your hand.

drop_by_lines: Qian left a parcel by your door: 'Not a sale, {player}. A friend's price is nothing at all. Tell no one.'
Qian slid something under your door with a ledger scrap: 'Entered under goodwill, {player}. Never to be repaid.'
lend_lines: Qian counts the day's takings and clears his throat. "A free pair of hands. I will not call it charity, {player}. I will call it goodwill."
"The stall ran smoother with you at it," Qian admits. "Do not tell the other brokers I said so."
npcs.graduation_line: Qian closes the abacus. "The finger is yours now, {player}. No more discount, no more lessons. Congratulations."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, I hear it is your birthday. Information costs, but this I give free: you are one year richer in days. Spend them well.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {festival} with you, {player}, and I forgot to count a single coin. Do not spread that around; it ruins my name.

festival_lines.mid_autumn_festival: Mid-Autumn, {player}: the one night I haggle for pleasure, not profit. Take a moon cake. No, no charge. Do not tell the others.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}. Even brokers are born, it seems. I will not charge you for today's gossip. Only today.
npcs.name: Broker Qian
npcs.title: Information Broker

tend_lines: Yun cleans the cut with wine from his gourd and ties it off with a torn sleeve. 'A scar is a lesson, {player}. Keep it.'
Yun sets his hand against your back and steadies your breath, the way the road taught him. 'Rest, {player}. The sword can wait.'

lessons.text: {name} rests a blade across your palms. "Hold it as you would a sleeping child. Firm, and without fear." You spend the morning on a single cut.
{name} sets a leaf on the wind and bids you split it. By dusk you have, once, and he nods as if it were nothing.

drop_by_lines: Yun left something by your gate: 'Found it on the path and thought of you, {player}. Keep your edge clean.'
Yun's note was short, pinned beneath the gift: 'For the road, {player}. Do not make a speech of it.'
lend_lines: Yun lets the last log fall in two clean halves. "You hold the blade steadier than most, {player}. Keep that."
"Wood does not argue," Yun says. "That is why I like it. Good work today, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a year older? Then your blade has had a year to learn you. Drink with me; the road can wait one evening.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {festival}. I do not usually stay for such days. I stayed, {player}. Do not make me say why.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: Qingming. I sweep one grave each spring and name no one aloud. Sit, {player}; the cold dumplings are decent this year.

npcs.birthday_line: Another year, another road. {player}, sit. A sword is a poor thing to celebrate with, but I have wine.
npcs.name: Yun Feng
npcs.title: Wandering Swordsman

tend_lines: Hua rolls a pill between two fingers and presses a bright salve to the wound. 'I made this for myself, {player}. Consider it spare.'
Hua tuts, tips a tincture over the hurt, and winds a bandage tight. 'An alchemist hates to watch good flesh waste, {player}.'
drop_by_lines: Hua left a small packet by your door: 'Left over from the furnace, {player}. Waste offends me.'
Hua set something at your door in a smudge of soot: 'Smoke and thanks, {player}. Come by soon.'
lend_lines: Hua waves smoke from her sleeve. "You watched the stall and did not once try to haggle. Rare, {player}. Thank you."
"A day away from the furnace," Hua sighs. "I forgot how pleasant it is to talk. Come again, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, happy birthday. No pill buys another year, I have tried. But the tea I brewed you is warm, and that is something.
npcs.festival_memory_line: I still taste {festival} on my tongue, {player}. Whatever we ate, it was better shared. I am writing it in my recipe notes.

festival_lines.mid_autumn_festival: {player}, I put a pinch of osmanthus in this year's moon cakes. Not medicine, I swear. Taste, and tell me the moon is brighter.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}, how did you know? Careful: a gift on the right day tastes sweeter than any pill I have brewed.

lessons.text: {name} lets you watch a full batch from first heat to last, and writes the settling of the clear-heart pill on a slip for you.
{name} taps the rim of the cauldron. "Healers' pills are patience. Here is how I draw the visceral mending pill, and why I never rush the fire."

npcs.name: Hua Qingyi
npcs.title: Wandering Alchemist

tend_lines: Xue binds the wound with a red silk ribbon, almost gently. 'Do not mistake this for kindness, {player}. I dislike waste.'
Xue licks her thumb, smears a bitter paste over the cut, and looks away. 'Tell no one I did this, {player}.'

lessons.text: {name} smiles and does not explain the red on her sleeve. "Pain is a teacher too. Breathe through it, little one." She sets a pouch in your hand.
{name} circles you slowly, then corrects your breath where it catches. "Do not flinch from what is warm. Use it."

drop_by_lines: Xue left it at your door without a knock: 'Do not read anything into it, {player}. It was in the way.'
Xue's note was one line: 'You have earned this, {player}. Do not make me say so twice.'
lend_lines: Xue turns a page and does not look up. "You sorted them correctly. Do not let it go to your head, {player}."
"Hmph. Quiet help is the only help I tolerate," Xue mutters. "You are tolerable, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}... they say today is yours. I do not do gifts. Take this: I remembered, and I will not say what it cost me.
npcs.birthday_line: Hmph. {player}. Do not look so pleased with yourself; you knowing the day means nothing. ...Stay anyway.
npcs.name: Xue Yao
npcs.title: Blood Lotus Disciple

tend_lines: Gu holds two fingers over the hurt until a slow warmth settles in. 'Old Azure Cloud trick, {player}. Call it a favor.'
Gu wraps the wound in cloud-pale cloth and hums something tuneless. 'Mountains mend slowly, {player}. So must you.'

lessons.text: {name} says nothing for an hour, then hands you a cup of pine tea. "Sit." You learn more from the stillness than from any word.
{name} walks you under the old pines at dawn. "Take what falls. The mountain gives needles to those who wait."

drop_by_lines: Gu left a small thing at your door and a note in shaky ink: 'The mountain gave more than I need, {player}.'
Gu's staff-print lay in the dust by your door, and beside it a gift: 'Old men remember kindness, {player}.'
lend_lines: Gu leans on his staff and eyes the swept ground. "My back thanks you, {player}. My pride does not, but it is old too."
"Slow work is good work," Gu wheezes. "You have the patience for it, {player}. Come again."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, your birthday, is it? Another ring on the pine. Sit; the clouds are good today and I have nobody else to tell.
npcs.festival_memory_line: I came down the mountain for {festival} and was glad of it, {player}. Company is a medicine I had forgotten to take.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: Qingming brings visitors to my mountain. Most ask for wisdom; you have brought dumplings. Sit, {player}, you are the wise one.

npcs.birthday_line: A birthday, {player}? At my age they come like mountain mist. Still, it is good that someone climbs up to see me.
npcs.name: Hermit Gu
npcs.title: Retired Azure Cloud Elder

tend_lines: Hei fishes a jar of grey ointment from his cart. 'Smells like the grave, {player}, but it knits flesh. Hold still.'
Hei wipes your wound with a rag he swears is clean and binds it hard. 'Cheap, fast and ugly, {player}. Like me.'

lessons.text: {name} drops his voice. "Where the cress grows thick, the water is sweet. Marsh folk know; outsiders don't." He pushes a bundle at you.
{name} shows you the firm ground between the reeds, one hop at a time, and laughs when you slip. "Now you will not drown, friend."

drop_by_lines: Hei left a parcel at your door: 'Hee! No charge, {player}. Do not spread it about, I have a name to keep.'
Hei tossed something onto your step: 'A friend's discount, {player}: all of it. Do not tell the marsh.'
lend_lines: Hei sweeps the last bone-charm into a pile. "You hawk almost as well as I do, {player}. Almost. Hei gives no discounts on praise."
"A busy stall is a lucky stall," Hei cackles. "You brought me luck today, {player}."
npcs.graduation_line: Hei spits happily over the side. "The reed bends, the reed stays. Nothing more I can sell you, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}! Birthday, eh? Hee. Nothing on my cart is a gift, but the company is free today. Don't tell the dead.
npcs.birthday_line: Ehe. {player} remembers the day the old peddler crawled out of the mud. Have a dry corner of my skiff.
npcs.name: Peddler Hei
npcs.title: Corpse Peddler

tend_lines: Bai tends the wound with a swift hand and does not meet your eye. 'The rules forbid gifts, {player}. They say nothing of bandages.'
Bai steadies your arm and circulates a thread of calm Qi through the hurt. 'Rest. That is advice, {player}, not a gift.'

lessons.text: {name} reddens, then shows you the first sword stance of the sect, slowly, three times over. "Do not tell Elder I showed you."
{name} spars with you until the sun is low, striking gently and talking the whole while about footwork.

lend_lines: Bai leans on her broom and looks over the clean stones. "The terrace has not been this tidy in a month, {player}."
"Sweeping is meditation with fewer excuses," Bai says, almost smiling. "Thank you, {player}."
npcs.graduation_line: Bai bows over her sword. "The moon has nothing left to teach you, {player}. Only you can carry it further."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, I heard it was your birthday. The sect forbids gifts between disciples, so this is only a feather I happened to find.
npcs.festival_memory_line: {player}! I am still smiling about {festival}. My seniors asked who I laughed with, and I said: a friend.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: {player}! The elders fly kites for the dead today. Mine is crooked, but I think my senior would have laughed at it.

npcs.birthday_line: {player}! The sect forgets such days, but you did not. I will practise my sword twice as long tomorrow.
npcs.name: Bai Qingwu
npcs.title: Azure Cloud Inner Disciple

tend_lines: Shen binds you with long pale fingers, as exactly as if counting coins. 'I keep my debtors alive, {player}. It is only sense.'
Shen sets a cold compress on the wound and says nothing for a long time. 'There is no ledger for this one, {player}.'

lessons.text: {name} leans over his counter. "Brush strokes, not ink, make the talisman. Take this paper and practise."
{name} tallies the market's moods on his fingers and teaches you when to sell and when to sit on your hands.

drop_by_lines: Shen left something by your door and a quiet note: 'I notice what you like, {player}. I remember everything.'
Shen's gift lay neatly on your step: 'A small kindness, {player}. I have entered nothing in my ledgers.'
lend_lines: Shen blinks slowly at the stall. "You tended my tables and read none of my ledgers. I noticed, {player}. I notice everything."
"Kindness without a price," Shen murmurs. "Unusual. I shall remember it, {player}, as I remember everything."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}. Today is your day, the ledgers say. I note it. I note everything. ...Happy birthday. That I do not note.
npcs.festival_memory_line: ...{festival} was loud, and I did not mind. That is your doing, {player}. Thank you for asking me along.

festival_lines.mid_autumn_festival: ...The moon is full and the stalls are loud. I like it better than silence tonight, {player}. Take a lantern.

npcs.birthday_line: ...Today, yes. Few notice. Take a seat, {player}; I will not ask what you want. Not today.
npcs.name: Shen Wuya
npcs.title: Hollow-Eyed Broker

tend_lines: Lin lays a palm over the hurt and the pain quiets like a bell damped by a hand. 'Go gently, {player}. The sect is young; so are you.'
Lin sends a slow thread of Qi through the wound, patient as a mountain stream. 'Rest, {player}. A founder must sometimes serve.'

lessons.text: {name} sets down his tea. "A sect is only as strong as its quietest disciple." He walks you through a breathing cycle his own master gave him.
{name} stands behind you through an entire night's meditation, saying nothing, and at dawn you find your qi runs smoother than it ever has.

drop_by_lines: Lin left a gift at your gate, no word: 'May it serve you well, {player},' reads the slip beneath.
Lin's attendant brought it by his word: 'A small thing from the old man, {player}. Walk well.'
lend_lines: Lin turns a page without opening his eyes. "Scrolls ordered, mind untroubled. A good day's work, {player}."
"The sect has a hundred hands," Lin says softly, "and still I notice yours, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a birthday is a small gate that opens once a year. Walk through it lightly. The Dao will wait for you on the other side.
npcs.festival_memory_line: A thousand peaks, and the sweetest hour of the season was {festival} at your side, {player}. Come, let an old man say thanks.

festival_lines.qingming_festival: Every spring I count the names we have lost and the young ones we gained. Fly a kite with me, {player}; they climb higher than I do.

npcs.birthday_line: Another spring over a thousand peaks, {player}. The young ones hide gifts behind their backs; you may do the same.
npcs.name: Patriarch Lin
npcs.title: Founding Patriarch of the Azure Cloud Sect

tend_lines: Gui cackles and dabs a smoking green paste on the wound. 'Do not scream, {player}. It frightens the lantern.'
Gui wraps the hurt in grave-cloth, wheezing a laugh. 'I have buried many who were hurt less, {player}. Live out of spite.'

lessons.text: {name} cackles. "Eat the bog catfish raw, boy! No? Hah. Then eat it cooked, like the weak." He flings you one and teaches you where they hide.
{name} drags you into the fog and shows you how to breathe where no one should. "Live a thousand years, learn a thousand tricks."

drop_by_lines: Gui left something by your door and cackled off into the reeds: 'Hee, old monsters pay their debts, {player}!'
Gui's gift sat on your step with a toothpick stuck in it: 'Do not look so surprised, {player}.'
lend_lines: Gui chuckles around his toothpick. "The lantern burns brighter when someone dusts the scrolls, {player}. Strange, that."
"Nobody helps an old monster," Gui rasps. "Yet here you are, {player}. Hee. Come back whenever."
npcs.player_birthday_line: Heh heh, {player}. Another year survived! The lanterns burn brighter for you tonight. I told them to. They obey me. Mostly.
npcs.birthday_line: Kekeke. {player}, you count my years? Then pour a cup for the ghosts, and one for me.
npcs.name: Old Monster Gui
npcs.title: Ghost-Lantern Old Monster

tend_lines: Ye drips a clear cloud-herb tincture into the wound and binds it light. 'The mountain air does half the work, {player}.'
Ye feeds you a small pill and dresses the hurt in one practiced motion. 'Walk it off slowly, {player}. No leaping from ridges.'

lessons.text: {name} lifts the lid on her cauldron and lets you smell the steam. "Fire is a mood. Learn it." She sends you off with a bundle of dew grass.
{name} corrects your wrist, your breath and your patience in a single afternoon, and her pill comes out clearer for it.

drop_by_lines: Ye left a small bundle by your door: 'It was drying too long to waste, {player}. Use it kindly.'
Ye's note was brisk beneath the gift: 'From my shelf to your hands, {player}. Mind the dose.'
lend_lines: Ye taps her ladle on the pot. "You sorted the herbs without being told which were poison. Wise, {player}."
"Many apprentices, many accidents," Ye says. "You have caused none today, {player}. Thank you."
npcs.graduation_line: Ye taps her spoon on the rim. "A rock does not need to be told it is a rock. Nothing left to teach, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, birthday! I could not find a cloud thick enough to wrap you a gift, so you have my good wishes and this warm pill.
npcs.birthday_line: The clouds were kind this morning, {player}, and now you are too. Even an alchemist can be pleased by a small gift.
npcs.name: Ye Zhuoran
npcs.title: Cloud-Walking Alchemist

tend_lines: Xuan presses a cold hand to the wound and the bleeding stops. 'A lord does not fuss, {player}. Consider this a debt withheld.'
Xuan glares, then rips a strip of dark cloth and binds you himself. 'Live, {player}. I dislike losing what I have chosen.'

lessons.text: {name} sits on his hall's stone seat and speaks for a long time of how a throne weighs. "Bear it lightly, or it breaks the back."
{name} calls you to the training yard and works you through the old form until your arms shake. "Again," he says, and then, "Better."

drop_by_lines: Xuan left a gift at your door: 'A lord gives without ceremony, {player}, when the giver is a friend.'
Xuan's servant set it by your gate: 'My lord says: take it, {player}, and say nothing.'
lend_lines: Xuan watches the work done and does not smile. "A willing hand. Rare in my hall, {player}. I will not forget it."
"Even a throne is grateful for a tidy floor," Xuan says dryly. "You did well, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}. Another year is another skull you have not yet become. Be glad. I raise a cup, which is more than I do for most.
npcs.birthday_line: Hah. {player}, a skull for every year, they say. You bring something less grim? Then you are welcome at my fire.
npcs.name: Xuan Moying
npcs.title: Hundred-Skull Lord

tend_lines: Lan lays her blade aside, cleans the wound, and binds it with quiet care. 'A sword is only as good as the arm, {player}. Rest yours.'
Lan breathes a calm Qi thread through the hurt. 'Feel it settle, {player}? That is stillness. Remember it.'

lessons.text: {name} hands you a plain wooden blade. "The edge matters little. The heart behind it does." You cut at the air until it sings.
{name} brushes snow from a flat stone and sits beside you. "No sword, no thought. Just the cold." The silence teaches you more.

drop_by_lines: Lan left a small gift at your door: 'The mountain air makes me generous, {player}. Do not mistake it for softness.'
Lan's note was a single clean line: 'From my table to yours, {player}. Walk the quiet road.'
lend_lines: Lan lifts the last split log and sets it down gently. "Wood has a grain, a road to follow. You found it, {player}."
"A sword-saint chops firewood badly," Lan admits. "You chop it well, {player}. My thanks."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, a year gone like a sword's flash. Do not mourn it. Stand, draw, and let this new year be sharper than the last.
npcs.birthday_line: I walk, I forget the date, and someone remembers it for me. Thank you, {player}. The road is lighter today.
npcs.name: Lan Zhiyuan
npcs.title: Wandering Sword-Saint

tend_lines: Wen mends the wound the way he mends stone, patiently, seam by seam. 'Nothing breaks that cannot be set right, {player}.'
Wen presses a poultice of mountain moss to the hurt. 'The ridge heals every scar eventually, {player}. So do we.'

lessons.text: {name} lifts a clod of earth and crumbles it. "Taste it." You do. "Now you know what the hill is made of." He gives you a sprig of highland thyme.
{name} presses your palm to the ground and has you feel the slow qi of the mountain until your own breath matches it.

drop_by_lines: Wen left a handful of grain by your door: 'The field gave, {player}. It would be rude to refuse a gift of the ground.'
Wen set something by your gate with soil still on it: 'Take it, {player}. A good harvest is meant to be passed on.'
lend_lines: Wen presses the earth flat with his palm. "The soil is glad of you, {player}, and so am I."
"A mountain mends one field at a time," Wen says. "Today you mended one with me, {player}."
npcs.player_birthday_line: {player}, happy birthday. A year is a fine stone to set in the wall of a life. Mind that you lay it straight, and lay it well.
npcs.birthday_line: {player}, the mountains have waited a long time for me to turn a year older. Sit; the mending can wait one day.
npcs.name: Wen Qingxu
npcs.title: Mountain-Mending Sage

errands.text: Elder Mo asked for 6 Spirit Herbs (the slope above Qingshi Village).
Herbalist Lan asked for 5 Qi Condensing Grass (Herb Patch, Misty Forest).
Hua Qingyi asked for 4 Qi Gathering Pills you made yourself.
Hermit Gu asked for 3 Cold Iron (the crystal vein, Azure Peak).
Peddler Hei asked for 3 Purple Cloud Mushrooms (Corpse-Lily Bog).
Patriarch Lin asked for 3 Ice Soul Flowers (Frost Ledge, Azure Peak).
Old Monster Gui asked for 3 Blood Ginseng (Corpse-Lily Bog, Withered Bone Marsh).
Ye Zhuoran asked for 3 Cloud Mist Orchids (Thunder-Struck Terraces, Myriad Peaks Ridge).
Bai Qingwu asked for 3 Nine-Leaf Soul Grass (Cloud-Sea Orchid Terraces, Azure Peak).
Shen Wuya asked for 2 Star Silver (Meteor Crater Field, Fallen Star Market).
Wen Qingxu asked for 2 Soul Infant Fruit (Thunder-Struck Terraces, Myriad Peaks Ridge).
Xuan Moying asked for a Soul Severing Lotus (it grows only where Nascent Soul cultivators can pick it).

scenes.text: {name} leads you to the rope swing behind her family's house, grey with rain now. "We were smaller than the knots, then," she laughs, and pushes you once, as she used to.
{name} insists you stay for supper. Nothing is said about why; the bowl is simply set down in front of you, full.
{name} pours you tea and, for once, does not lecture. "I spent sixty years chasing the heavens," the old cultivator says. "Sit. The kettle teaches patience better than I ever did."
{name} shows you a pale scar across the wrist and tells how it was earned, and what it cost a friend. "Do not repeat my mistakes. Make your own, smaller ones."
{name} hangs a paper lantern at her gate and writes your name beside hers on it. "For a good road," she says, a little pink, and presses a second lantern into your hands.
{name} walks you along the ridge path and shows how he sets a snare: patient hands, no hurry. "The wood tells you everything, if you stop talking," he grunts, and hands you a strip of smoked meat.
{name} lets you hold his old bow, the grip worn smooth by twenty winters. "I never lent it to anyone," he mutters, then nods once, which from him is a speech.
{name} sees you passing and calls up from the ladder. You hold it steady while the thatch is patched, and nobody mentions payment, only a nod of thanks.
{name} tells you how the village looked before the stone road: wolves in the barley and a sky full of crows. "We got by," they say. "People do."
{name} presses a bundle into your arms at the lane's end. "You came when the well ran dry and when the fever came. This is the least of it."
{name} spreads her morning's gathering across a flat stone and names each plant for you, root first, then leaf. "Learn the roots," she says. "Leaves lie. Roots remember where they grew."

{name} is quiet over the drying rack. "I came into this forest to bury a sickness I could not cure," she says at last. "Now I only gather what might cure the next one." She keeps her eyes on the herbs, and you let her.
{name} sits on a log sharpening a thin red blade, and does not tell you to go. "Most people leave once they smell the sect on me," she says. "You have stood here a whole hour. Strange."

{name} turns the blade over and over in the half light. "The sect took me in when I was nine and hungry," she says flatly. "It never once asked if I was kind. You are the first who did." She sheathes it and looks away.
{name} unrolls a stained cloth and lets you pick through the trinkets without a word of haggling. "These are honest bones," the peddler wheezes. "Cheap, and no ghost in them. Mostly."

{name} sits down on the cart shaft and takes off the grimy hat. "Forty years pushing this thing through the marsh," the old peddler says. "The dead are poor company but they never owe me money. You, I think I will miss."

{name} floats a pale lantern between you and the reeds. "The little lights are only the lost," the old monster murmurs. "I keep them company. Do not look so pleased, child; it is not kindness, it is habit."

{name} is silent a long while, the lantern guttering low. "I had a disciple once. She laughed like you do, before I fed her to the canon." A dry rattle, perhaps a laugh. "Remember that, when you think me gentle."
{name} slides a cup of cold tea across the counter and, for once, writes nothing down. "Free," the broker says. "Do not tell the street. A man in my trade cannot be seen giving things away."

{name} closes the ledger and leaves it closed. "Everyone in this market owes me a secret," Qian says. "I have never told anyone the one I owe. It is about a daughter." The smile is small, and tired, and not for sale.
{name} lets you stir the pot, then frowns at your wrist and fixes your grip. "Slower. A pill is only a fire that was persuaded, never ordered." A pause. "Better. Do it again."

{name} sets down a cracked cauldron lid you have never seen used. "My first. It exploded on the seventh day and took my eyebrows," Hua says with a small grin. "I kept the lid. Everything I know began with that bang."
{name} watches the crowd with hollow eyes and does not turn when you stop beside the stall. "You walk like someone who has nothing to sell," the broker says. "That is rarer here than gold."

{name} speaks to the lane rather than to you. "I sold a man's name once for a handful of jade. He was my brother." A long breath. "I tell you because you will not repeat it, and because I wanted one person to know."
{name} brings a lamp and sits with you through the dark hours, saying little. At dawn the lamp is trimmed and the tea is hot: that is how friends are made here.
